clue.text: Essential spaniel's in bed after going walkies

indicators.note: a thing gone walkies has wandered off or gone astray, so these letters are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: the dog's word with its S, read here as spaniels
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog owner decides that a walk is vital once the spaniel has been lying in its bed all day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: the anagram of SPANIELSINBED, signalled by 'going walkies' (British slang for wandering off), gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one cannot do without is vital or necessary, the same sense as essential.

clue.text: They roll up and after opening up they clean up

definitions.text: They roll up and after opening up they clean up

parts.words: They roll up and after opening up they clean up
parts.note: table linen is rolled into rings for the meal, then unfolded to wipe diners' mouths and fingers

explanation.surface: Seems to describe people arriving, getting going and then making a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth or paper squares at the table are rolled up and, once unfolded, used to wipe hands and lips clean.

clue.text: Aide contrived plan

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An assistant has devised a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or scheme is a thought of what to do, a common synonym for a notion.

clue.text: Complete the course and get dead drunk

definitions.meaning: to graduate from a training course, especially at a military academy

explanation.surface: A student finishes college and celebrates far too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both graduating from training, as cadets do, and collapsing unconscious from drink.

clue.text: Once more put up half rain falls

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is written from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: once more means again

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word rain is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Seems to say the rain has eased to half its strength and is coming down once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border, so the place-name stands for falls.

clue.text: Unidentified girl accepts ring

indicators.note: accepts means the girl's name takes the ring inside itself

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A mystery woman agrees to a proposal and takes the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for anonymous, it marks a person or author whose name is unknown.

clue.text: Unauthorised disclosure over time causes a loss in liquid assets

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an unauthorised disclosure of information is a leak
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A whistleblower's revelations gradually damage a company's cash position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid assets' suggests money, but the definition is literal: liquid escaping from a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the loss of fluid through a hole or crack, a playful reading of liquid assets.

clue.text: Saw the differences and celebrated

definitions.meaning: told things apart, discerned what separated them

explanation.surface: Someone noticed the contrasts and threw a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb in the past tense means told apart; the adjective means eminent or renowned.

clue.text: Disdainful prisoner being sent down

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
going downwards; also playing on 'sent down' meaning jailed

explanation.surface: A scornful convict is being jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being patronising means treating others as inferior, which is a disdainful, superior manner.

clue.text: Simpers, out to influence

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone simpers, aiming to win people over.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a mark on someone, so as to sway their opinion, is to influence them.

clue.text: Head off disaster going to a party with fruit

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: havoc is widespread destruction, a disaster
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Seems to advise averting catastrophe by taking fruit along to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' reads as 'prevent', but here it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear-shaped green-skinned avocado is botanically a fruit, a large berry with a single stone.

clue.text: Willowy spruce

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of a slender fir tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means slender in build and also neat and tidy in appearance.

clue.text: Mr Runyan has a setback — he's domestically unstable

indicators.note: a setback sends the name back, so it is written in reverse

parts.note: Damon Runyon was the American writer of Broadway stories such as Guys and Dolls (spelt Runyan here)

explanation.surface: Seems to say a writer suffered a reverse and his home life is in turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no settled home is unstable in the domestic sense, a playful description.

clue.text: Shakespeare is forbidden, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: something forbidden is barred

explanation.surface: A claim that Shakespeare's works are banned, or so it is rumoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is known as the Bard of Avon, a bard being a poet.

clue.text: It goes to the head of Basques and servicemen

definitions.text: It goes to the head of Basques and servicemen

parts.words: It goes to the head of Basques and servicemen
parts.note: a flat round cap is worn on the head by Basque people and by soldiers

explanation.surface: Seems to be about something that leads Basques and soldiers, or rises to their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to the head' suggests intoxication or leadership, but it means is worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft flat cap is traditional Basque headwear and part of many military uniforms.

clue.text: In time about to get on together

indicators.note: In means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: an age is a period of time
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Seems to say that eventually two people will come round to getting along.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on together is to be in harmony, to concur and see eye to eye.

clue.text: Eton was upset? It's not a problem!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off the news that Eton, the famous school, was distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal reply means something is easy, no trouble at all.

clue.text: Sportsmen seen at the bank

parts.note: fishermen sit on a river bank, not in a financial institution

explanation.surface: Athletes spotted at a high-street bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank is a riverbank, not a place for money.
explanation.definitionFit: People who fish with rod and line are sportsmen who sit on a riverbank.

clue.text: Economise in vain

definitions.meaning: read as two words, to consume a smaller amount

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word tells you to consume a smaller amount; whole, it means futile or without effect.

clue.text: Building seen from both ends of editor's office

indicators.note: both ends means only the opening and closing letters of the phrase are kept, the middle dropped

explanation.surface: A building visible from either end of the editor's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ends of' keeps EDI from the start and FICE from the finish of the phrase, dropping TORSOF in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing structure, a grand word for a building.

clue.text: Well directed, it may finish off the game

definitions.text: Well directed, it may finish off the game

parts.words: Well directed, it may finish off the game
parts.note: game here is wild birds or animals shot for sport, killed by a well-aimed gun

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a well-managed sports match being brought to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests a match; it means hunted animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-bore gun firing pellets is used to shoot pheasant and other game birds.

clue.text: Act as chairman, but show partiality in advance?

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before or in advance
to side with someone is to take their part

explanation.surface: Seems to accuse a chairman of having made up his mind before the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman runs a meeting, which is to be in charge and conduct proceedings.

clue.text: Extract from part of a book about a ship

indicators.note: about means the page goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a page is part of a book
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An excerpt from a chapter about a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A short section quoted from a text is an excerpt or extract.

clue.text: Silver in one place of gold — just fancy

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: in means silver is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: gold is dug from a mine
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Surprise at silver turning up in a gold mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'Just fancy!' expresses surprise, as does 'Picture that!' or 'Who'd have thought!'.

clue.text: Error one should catch?

definitions.meaning: a fielder standing beside the wicketkeeper in cricket, placed to catch edged balls

explanation.definitionFit: A minor mistake is a lapse, and in cricket a close fielder behind the batter, next to the wicketkeeper, has the same name.

clue.text: Computer operator gets instant employment

parts.note: a mo is a moment or instant
use means employment, as in putting something to work

explanation.surface: Someone working with computers lands a job straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operator' suggests a person, but it is the device that operates the computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hand-held pointing device moves the cursor and operates a computer.

clue.text: Bananas four inches in measure

definitions.meaning: a bunch of bananas growing together on the stem
a unit of four inches used to measure horses' height

explanation.definitionFit: A cluster of bananas has this name, and horses are measured in units of four inches by this word.

clue.text: Settled business

definitions.meaning: fixed, definite, not liable to change

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means fixed or definite; the noun means a company.

clue.text: Experts in cards

definitions.meaning: the top cards of each suit in a pack

explanation.definitionFit: Highly skilled people are called this, and the same word names the single-pip cards in a pack.

clue.text: Finishing playing one's part

definitions.meaning: leaving or departing at the end
an actor walking offstage as the script directs

explanation.definitionFit: Departing marks the end of something, and an actor leaving the stage is following a stage direction in the play.

clue.text: Where lots are put up only to be knocked down

definitions.text: Where lots are put up only to be knocked down

parts.words: Where lots are put up only to be knocked down
parts.note: items for sale are offered to bidders and sold with the fall of the hammer

explanation.surface: Sounds like a building site where structures are erected and then demolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked down' means sold to a bidder with a stroke of the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: At a public sale, lots are offered to bidders and knocked down to the highest one.

clue.text: Bug set off a nameless illness

parts.note: a bug is a germ

indicators.note: set off means started moving or exploded, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect triggers an unidentified disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella, a mild viral infection that causes a rash, is the illness known by this name.
